Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

  "narrative": "This first registration wave prioritizes high-confidence biomarker-to-dependency relationships in the supplied lung cell-line CRISPR screen dataset. For MAPK/RAS-related oncogenic drivers, I test the expected selective dependency: KRAS mutations should associate with stronger KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E with stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification with stronger EGFR dependency; and ERBB2 amplification with stronger ERBB2 dependency. For chromatin and DNA-repair dependencies, SMARCA4 loss is a canonical context for SMARCA2 dependency, and MSI-high is a strong context for WRN dependency. For MDM2 and USP7, I compare TP53 wild-type (tp53_loss=0) versus TP53 loss (tp53_loss=1), with the hypothesis that wild-type TP53 cells may show stronger dependency on p53-pathway regulators through USP7-MDM2-p53 circuitry, although direction is left as a testable hypothesis. record.narrative: This first registration wave prioritizes high-confidence biomarker-to-dependency relationships in the supplied lung cell-line CRISPR screen dataset. For MAPK/RAS-related oncogenic drivers, I test the expected selective dependency: KRAS mutations should associate with stronger KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E with stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification with stronger EGFR dependency; and ERBB2 amplification with stronger ERBB2 dependency. For chromatin and DNA-repair dependencies, SMARCA4 loss is a canonical context for SMARCA2 dependency, and MSI-high is a strong context for WRN dependency. For MDM2 and USP7, I compare TP53 wild-type (tp53_loss=0) versus TP53 loss (tp53_loss=1), with the hypothesis that wild-type TP53 cells may show stronger dependency on p53-pathway regulators through USP7-MDM2-p53 circuitry, although direction is left as a testable hypothesis. MYC amplification is used for broad transcription/translation-associated dependencies (POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9), based on the prior that MYC-driven cells have heightened transcriptional and ribosome-biogenesis demands. KEAP1 loss is tested against NFE2L2 dependency because loss of KEAP1 activates NRF2/NFE2L2 pathway signaling and may alter selective dependency. All proposed comparisons are pre-registered as unresolved, because no dataset evidence has yet been returned. The direction is coded as -1 because more negative dependency scores mean stronger dependency; the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative under the proposed biology. A signed estimate will support stronger dependency when it is positive under this coding. I will assess both the magnitude relative to the 10% threshold and the 95% Welch uncertainty, while keeping claims limited to associations in this dataset.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

  "narrative": "All 12 discovery results are valid under the 20-observation cell rule and have Welch intervals signed to the registered hypothesis direction. Because direction is -1 for all original claims, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a more negative (stronger) dependency in the exposed group, whereas a negative signed estimate corresponds to weaker dependency. To judge the 10% clinical-significance threshold, I used a rough comparator-mean relative benchmark from the outcome mean and cell proportions. For the main outcomes around -0.25, a 10% threshold is approximately 0.025 dependency-score units; for outcomes with near-zero overall means (NFE2L2 and USP7), relative thresholds must be interpreted carefully, but absolute effects above 0.75 are extremely large and unambiguous. H6 (SMARCA2: SMARCA4 loss vs intact, signed +0.784, 95% CI +0.765 to +0.803) and H7 (WRN: MSI-high vs MSI-low, signed +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.819) show very large, precise associations in the expected stronger-dependency direction and should be accepted as dataset-supported associations. H12 (USP7: TP53 wild-type vs TP53 loss, signed +0.802, CI +0.782 to +0.822) is also huge and precise, indicating much stronger USP7 dependency in TP53 wild-type cells than in TP53-loss cells; this is accepted as a dataset association, though causal interpretation requires validation and confounding assessment. H8 is opposite to the registered KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2-dependency direction: signed estimate -0.796 (CI -0.816 to -0.776) means KEAP1-loss cells have much weaker NFE2L2 dependency (less negative scores), not stronger; thus H8 is rejected and a reversed claim is registered. H2, H9, H10, and H11 show no clinically meaningful support in the expected direction; their upper signed bounds fall below an approximately 10% threshold, so they are rejected. H1, H3, H4, and H5 remain unresolved because their intervals include both null/contrary effects and values near or above the 10% benchmark. H3 is the strongest unresolved driver-specific effect (EGFR amplification vs EGFR dependency, signed +0.025, CI nearly from 0 to +0.051) and is biologically plausible but imprecise; I request independent validation for H3 because a clean positive result would justify acceptance, while a null or negative validation would justify rejection. Multiple comparisons were considered: the accepted effects are so far beyond uncertainty and the clinical threshold that they are not plausibly explained by 12 tests alone, whereas the borderline effects are being treated conservatively. Current conclusions are limited to this supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR dataset and do not prove causality or generalizability.",

record.narrative: All 12 discovery results are valid under the 20-observation cell rule and have Welch intervals signed to the registered hypothesis direction. Because direction is -1 for all original claims, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a more negative (stronger) dependency in the exposed group, whereas a negative signed estimate corresponds to weaker dependency. To judge the 10% clinical-significance threshold, I used a rough comparator-mean relative benchmark from the outcome mean and cell proportions. For the main outcomes around -0.25, a 10% threshold is approximately 0.025 dependency-score units; for outcomes with near-zero overall means (NFE2L2 and USP7), relative thresholds must be interpreted carefully, but absolute effects above 0.75 are extremely large and unambiguous. H6 (SMARCA2: SMARCA4 loss vs intact, signed +0.784, 95% CI +0.765 to +0.803) and H7 (WRN: MSI-high vs MSI-low, signed +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.819) show very large, precise associations in the expected stronger-dependency direction and should be accepted as dataset-supported associations. H12 (USP7: TP53 wild-type vs TP53 loss, signed +0.802, CI +0.782 to +0.822) is also huge and precise, indicating much stronger USP7 dependency in TP53 wild-type cells than in TP53-loss cells; this is accepted as a dataset association, though causal interpretation requires validation and confounding assessment. H8 is opposite to the registered KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2-dependency direction: signed estimate -0.796 (CI -0.816 to -0.776) means KEAP1-loss cells have much weaker NFE2L2 dependency (less negative scores), not stronger; thus H8 is rejected and a reversed claim is registered. H2, H9, H10, and H11 show no clinically meaningful support in the expected direction; their upper signed bounds fall below an approximately 10% threshold, so they are rejected. H1, H3, H4, and H5 remain unresolved because their intervals include both null/contrary effects and values near or above the 10% benchmark. H3 is the strongest unresolved driver-specific effect (EGFR amplification vs EGFR dependency, signed +0.025, CI nearly from 0 to +0.051) and is biologically plausible but imprecise; I request independent validation for H3 because a clean positive result would justify acceptance, while a null or negative validation would justify rejection. Multiple comparisons were considered: the accepted effects are so far beyond uncertainty and the clinical threshold that they are not plausibly explained by 12 tests alone, whereas the borderline effects are being treated conservatively. Current conclusions are limited to this supplied lung-cell-line CRISPR dataset and do not prove causality or generalizability.

record.narrative: Synthesis of iteration 1: the only due response is validation R13 for H3, EGFR amplification versus stronger EGFR dependency. The claim direction is signed so that a positive estimate corresponds to a more negative, stronger dependency in EGFR-amplified cells. Discovery R3 was borderline positive and imprecise, estimate +0.0252 with a 95 percent interval -0.0003 to +0.0507; relative to the comparator mean around -0.25, a 10 percent clinically significant difference is roughly 0.025 dependency-score units. Independent validation R13 was small and opposite to the hypothesis, estimate -0.0070, with a wide independent interval -0.0487 to +0.0347 under the stricter validation alpha. The validation therefore fails to corroborate the borderline discovery effect, and the combined evidence does not support a scientifically meaningful EGFR-amplification association with EGFR dependency in this dataset. I reject H3 and close this specific main-effect claim, but this rejection means the supplied dataset does not support the registered association, not that EGFR amplification can never affect EGFR dependency in other contexts. Overall supported dataset findings are H6 SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H7 MSI-high associated with stronger WRN dependency, H12 TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss associated with stronger USP7 dependency, and H13 the reversed NFE2L2 claim, where KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency rather than stronger dependency. H6, H7, and H12/H13 have huge absolute effects with narrow intervals, far exceeding the relative 10 percent benchmark for outcomes with mean dependency near -0.25; for USP7 and NFE2L2, where overall means are near zero, relative percentage interpretation is less stable, but the absolute effects of about 0.78 to 0.80 dependency-score units are unambiguous within the dataset. Negative or unsupported findings include H2 BRAF V600E versus stronger BRAF dependency, H8 original KEAP1-loss direction for stronger NFE2L2 dependency, H9 through H11 MYC amplification versus stronger RPL11, POLR2A, or DHX9 dependency, and now H3 EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency after validation. Unresolved uncertainty remains mainly for H1 KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency, H4 ERBB2 amplification versus ERBB2 dependency, and H5 TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss for MDM2 dependency; each has some positive signal but intervals include null and clinically modest effects, so none is accepted. The next most informative analyses should analyze already registered refinements H14 through H23, especially context specificity for the accepted strong effects and the ARID1A-SMARCA2 comparison. If a refined effect is precise, crosses the 10 percent threshold, and is biologically coherent, independent validation would then be useful. All conclusions are limited to associations in the supplied lung cell-line CRISPR dataset and do not establish causality or clinical generalizability.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Iteration 2 explore focuses on three scientific needs: context-specific robustness of the already accepted strong dependency associations, resolution of borderline MAPK driver claims after the initial broad tests, and a small expansion into biologically motivated DNA-repair/chromatin contexts. First, I register main-effect refinements for the accepted strong effects within adenocarcinoma: SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 wild-type versus TP53-loss for USP7 dependency, KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency under the reversed direction, and MSI-high versus WRN dependency. These are absolute subgroup effect checks rather than interaction tests; they are useful because a large accepted effect could be diluted, concentrated, or absent in the largest lineage subtype. Second, I register pure-context refinements for MAPK dependencies. The broad KRAS and ERBB2 effects remain unresolved, and the broad BRAF test was negative. Excluding alternative MAPK pathway drivers may reveal a cleaner oncogene-selective effect if the prior nulls were diluted by mixed driver biology. This remains hypothesis generation in the supplied dataset, not a causal test. Third, I add an ARID1A-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency test restricted to SMARCA4-intact cells, which asks whether a second BAF subunit loss marks SMARCA2 dependency independently of the canonical SMARCA4-loss context. Finally, I add a technical robustness check for SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency within the dominant Avana library and a biologically motivated WRN context using BRCA2 loss. These proposals are registered as unresolved because they are new comparisons. Direction coding follows the established convention: direction -1 means a positive signed estimate corresponds to a more negative dependency score in the exposed group, while direction +1 means a positive signed estimate corresponds to a less negative/stronger raw score in the exposed group. For NFE2L2, the reversed accepted finding used direction +1 because KEAP1 loss appeared to weaken dependency, so subtype-robustness claims keep that sign.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger, more negative dependency in the exposed group; for H26, direction +1 and positive signed estimate mean a less negative, weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells, consistent with the previously accepted reversed direction. I compared each effect against a rough 10% comparator-mean benchmark: outcomes with mean dependency around -0.25 to -0.31 imply absolute thresholds near 0.025 to 0.030, while near-zero outcomes such as USP7 and NFE2L2 should be judged primarily by absolute dependency-score differences because relative percentages become unstable. H24 adenocarcinoma SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency, H25 adenocarcinoma TP53 wild-type versus TP53-loss versus USP7 dependency, H26 adenocarcinoma KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H27 adenocarcinoma MSI-high versus WRN dependency, and H32 Avana-library SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency all have enormous absolute effects around +0.78 to +0.80 with lower bounds still far above any plausible 10% benchmark. These accept the context-specific extensions of the already supported dataset findings and show that the main effects are not diluted in adenocarcinoma or the dominant Avana library. H31 shows no independent ARID1A-loss association with SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-intact cells: signed estimate -0.003, CI -0.025 to +0.019, so ARID1A is not supported as a separate BAF-loss marker in this dataset. H33 BRCA2-loss versus WRN is essentially null, estimate -0.00008, but the interval is wide because BRCA2 loss is rare and reaches above a possible 10% positive benchmark, so I leave it unresolved but deferred. H28 pure MAPK-driver KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency remains borderline positive but imprecise, estimate +0.013, CI -0.007 to +0.033; excluding BRAF, EGFR, and ERBB2 drivers did not resolve the broader KRAS claim. H30 pure ERBB2 amplification versus ERBB2 dependency is opposite to the expected direction with upper signed bound below the rough 10% benchmark, so I reject that specific claim. H16 adenocarcinoma TP53 wild-type versus TP53-loss for MDM2 is small and imprecise, estimate +0.016, CI -0.014 to +0.046; it supports neither acceptance nor a confident null. H19 RB1-loss versus KIF18A is small positive but imprecise and remains unresolved. H21 KRAS mutation versus RIT1 dependency is small and opposite to expected with upper bound well below the benchmark, so I reject it. The multiple-comparison burden across the first 24 main-effect tests does not credibly explain the very large accepted effects, whereas the small MAPK and MDM2 effects should remain cautious. I request independent validation for H1 broad KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency because it is the most biologically important remaining unresolved driver dependency and pure-context KRAS evidence did not settle it.

record.narrative: Synthesis of validation for H1: broad KRAS mutation versus stronger KRAS dependency. The registered direction is negative for the raw difference, so a positive signed estimate means a more negative, stronger KRAS dependency in KRAS-mutant cells, whereas a negative signed estimate means weaker KRAS dependency in KRAS-mutant cells. Discovery R1 was a small positive but imprecise association, estimate +0.0137 with 95 percent interval -0.0038 to +0.0312. Using the overall dependency_KRAS mean around -0.245, a 10 percent relative clinical benchmark is approximately 0.0245 dependency-score units, so the discovery estimate itself was below the benchmark and only its upper bound crossed it. Independent validation R26 was in the opposite direction, estimate -0.0152, with an independent interval -0.0417 to +0.0112 under the stricter validation threshold. The validation upper bound is below the approximate 10 percent clinical benchmark and the point estimate is opposite to the hypothesized stronger-dependency direction. Combining a null-to-small discovery estimate with a validation result that does not corroborate and fails to exclude the opposite or null pattern, the supplied dataset does not support a scientifically meaningful association between KRAS mutation and stronger KRAS dependency. Therefore H1 is rejected and closed. This rejection is limited to the supplied dataset and does not prove that KRAS mutation cannot matter in other contexts; it also leaves the pure MAPK-driver context H28 unresolved because excluding alternative MAPK drivers may still be biologically useful. The broader dataset conclusions now stand as follows. Supported strong dataset associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency, TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss with stronger USP7 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency. These are supported by very large absolute effects and narrow intervals. Context checks accepted adenocarcinoma specificity for SMARCA2, USP7, NFE2L2, and WRN, and accepted Avana-library robustness for SMARCA2. Negative or unsupported findings include broad BRAF V600E and EGFR amplification effects, EGFR amplification after validation, broad KRAS mutation after validation, MYC amplification effects on RPL11, POLR2A, and DHX9, ARID1A independent of SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2 dependency, pure ERBB2 amplification on ERBB2 dependency, KRAS mutation on RIT1 dependency, and the original KEAP1-loss direction for stronger NFE2L2 dependency. Unresolved areas include broad ERBB2 amplification, TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss for MDM2 dependency in broad and adenocarcinoma contexts, RB1 loss with KIF18A, BRCA2 loss with WRN, pure-context KRAS mutation, and several registered but untested context or biologically motivated comparisons. Next analyses should prioritize technical and biological robustness of the accepted large effects, including non-Avana library checks, lineage interactions, and the pure-context KRAS and BRAF refinements, before expanding into less coherent marker screens.

record.narrative: No discovery or validation assessments are due, so this explore stage registers new hypotheses that follow the strongest leads from iteration 2 rather than repeating completed tests. The accepted large dataset associations are still the highest-priority targets for context and technical robustness checks, because their magnitude far exceeds the approximate 10 percent relative benchmark and we now want to know whether they are diluted by lineage, library, or co-occurring DNA-repair contexts. I therefore add Avana-library robustness checks for WRN and USP7, an Avana-library check for the reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 finding, and a BRCA2-intact restriction for MSI-high WRN to test whether the WRN association is not simply carried by BRCA2-loss cases. The previously registered non-Avana checks for SMARCA2, USP7, and NFE2L2 complement these. I also add adenocarcinoma-restricted KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency because broad and validation KRAS evidence was null or opposite, but a lineage-specific context could still matter. For the unresolved p53/MDM2 question, I register Avana and non-Avana library restrictions plus a lineage interaction because broad and adenocarcinoma estimates are small and imprecise; these checks may reveal whether the weak TP53 wild-type effect is context-specific or essentially absent. For broader biologically motivated exploration, I add MTAP loss versus SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-intact cells as a co-deletion/chromatin-metabolic marker follow-up to the null ARID1A result, PIK3CA mutation versus STAT3 dependency as a PI3K-AKT-STAT3 signaling hypothesis, and ERBB2 amplification versus TMED10 dependency as a receptor-tyrosine kinase trafficking/secretory-pathway hypothesis. Direction coding follows the task convention: for mean differences, direction -1 means a positive signed estimate corresponds to a more negative, stronger dependency score in the exposed group relative to comparator, while direction +1 means a positive signed estimate corresponds to a less negative, weaker dependency score; interaction claims use the same signed-direction convention for the raw contrast. These proposals remain dataset associations and do not assume causality or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 3/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All newly delivered discovery estimates are valid under the cell-count rule and are interpreted using the sign conventions attached to each registered claim. For the direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger, more negative dependency in the exposed or TP53 wild-type group; for the direction +1 NFE2L2 claims, a positive signed estimate means weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells. H34, H37, H38, H43, H45, H46, and H44 all show effects near +0.77 to +0.81 with lower bounds still far above any plausible 10% benchmark or absolute dependency-scale benchmark. These accept the context-specific extensions of the already supported major associations: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 remains in non-Avana libraries, TP53 wild-type/USP7 remains in both Avana and non-Avana libraries, KEAP1-loss/weaker NFE2L2 remains in both library contexts, MSI-high/WRN remains in Avana libraries, and the MSI-high/WRN association remains essentially unchanged when BRCA2-loss cells are excluded. Although some non-Avana cells are smaller, they satisfy the 20-observation requirement and the intervals are still decisively large. I close these context checks because they have resolved the specific technical or co-occurring-marker robustness questions. The lineage interactions H14, H15, H35, and H36 are all near zero relative to their corresponding main effects, which are approximately 0.78. Their point estimates range from about -0.010 to -0.028 and their 95% intervals cross zero. This gives no positive evidence that adenocarcinoma versus non-adenocarcinoma context materially changes the accepted associations. However, because the intervals are wide enough to prevent a confident null-equivalence conclusion, especially for rare non-adenocarcinoma MSI-high cells, I leave these interaction claims unresolved but defer further investigation. H40, the Avana-library MDM2 TP53 wild-type comparison, is small and imprecise: signed estimate +0.013 with interval -0.013 to +0.039. With dependency_MDM2 mean around -0.27, a rough 10% absolute benchmark is about 0.027, so the point estimate is below the clinical benchmark and the interval includes both null and a possible small effect. I leave H40 active while waiting for H41 non-Avana MDM2 and H42 MDM2 lineage-interaction evidence. From a critical-review perspective, the very large accepted effects are not plausibly explained by multiple comparisons, and the context checks reduce the likelihood that they are artifacts of lineage or library distribution. They remain dataset associations, not causal claims. I am not requesting validation now because the accepted effects are already overwhelming across independent contexts, while the borderline small effects would likely be difficult to settle with one strict independent validation unless additional discovery contexts show a consistent near-threshold pattern.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

record.narrative: Synthesis of due validation: H3 broad EGFR amplification versus stronger EGFR dependency now has independent validation. The hypothesis direction is -1, so a positive signed estimate means EGFR-amplified cells have more negative, stronger EGFR dependency. Discovery R3 was borderline: signed estimate +0.0252 with 95 percent interval -0.0003 to +0.0507. Using the overall dependency_EGFR mean around -0.2495, a 10 percent relative benchmark is about 0.025 dependency units, so the discovery estimate was only marginally above that benchmark and its interval included null. Independent validation R13 was opposite, signed estimate -0.0070 with a stricter independent interval -0.0487 to +0.0347. Although the validation upper bound still crosses the approximate clinical benchmark, the independent point estimate does not corroborate the hypothesized stronger-dependency direction and is small in the opposite direction. Combining a borderline discovery result with a non-replicating, opposite validation estimate, the supplied dataset does not support a scientifically meaningful positive association between EGFR amplification and stronger EGFR dependency. H3 therefore remains rejected and closed as a supported dataset claim. This rejection is not a proof that EGFR amplification never affects EGFR dependency in other datasets or contexts, but it removes support for the broad EGFR-amplification claim in this dataset. H24 adenocarcinoma SMARCA4 loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency is independently validated. Discovery R14 was signed +0.777 with interval +0.755 to +0.799; validation R39 was signed +0.816 with a much stricter interval +0.780 to +0.852. Both are vastly larger than the roughly 10 percent benchmark implied by the SMARCA2 mean around -0.415, which is about 0.042 dependency units. H24 is accepted and closed. This strongly corroborates the broad SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association and shows that the association is robust in the adenocarcinoma context. The main supported dataset conclusions are now: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, with broad, adenocarcinoma-specific, Avana-library, non-Avana-library, and independent validation support; MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, with broad, adenocarcinoma, Avana-library, and BRCA2-intact support; TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency, with broad, adenocarcinoma, Avana-library, and non-Avana-library support; and KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency, with broad, adenocarcinoma, Avana-library, and non-Avana-library support. Major negative or unsupported claims remain: broad KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency, broad BRAF V600E versus BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency, MYC amplification effects on RPL11, POLR2A, and DHX9, KRAS mutation versus RIT1 dependency, pure ERBB2 amplification versus ERBB2 dependency, ARID1A loss independent of SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency, and the original KEAP1-loss direction for stronger NFE2L2 dependency. Unresolved areas include broad ERBB2 amplification, TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss for MDM2 dependency across broad, adenocarcinoma, and library contexts, RB1 loss versus KIF18A, BRCA2 loss versus WRN, pure-context KRAS mutation, pure-context BRAF, lineage interactions for the large effects, and several registered but untested biologically motivated marker-outcome comparisons. The most informative next analyses are to complete the TP53/MDM2 context set with H41 and H42, then test driver-context refinements such as H39 adenocarcinoma KRAS and H29 pure-context BRAF, and then proceed to broader marker screens such as H47 MTAP/SMARCA2, H48 PIK3CA/STAT3, H49 ERBB2/TMED10, and remaining active untested outcome-marker hypotheses. Independent validation is best conserved for borderline or context-specific claims after discovery contexts show consistent near-threshold signals, rather than spending more validation on the already overwhelming large effects.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

These proposals remain dataset associations and do not assume causality or external generalizability.","analyze":"No evidence assessments are currently due, so this analyze stage requests 12 already-registered analyses that can materially update the strongest dataset conclusions and begin resolving the unresolved TP53/MDM2 question.
